payload.rationale: The YES event requires NASA GISS’s reported, unsmoothed annual Land-Ocean Temperature Index for 2026 to strictly exceed both 1.28°C and its 2025 value. Equality does not qualify. I estimate a 25% chance using general climate background, not current-year observations. Continued human-caused warming increases the likelihood of new annual records, but year-to-year ocean variability remains important. The exceptional warmth associated with the 2023–2024 El Niño means that continued warming alone does not guarantee another record in 2026. My estimate assumes ordinary interannual variability around a rising temperature baseline; it does not assume a known 2026 ENSO state. The unknown 2025 value could also raise the effective hurdle above 1.28°C. The estimate could be too high if 2026 has substantial La Niña-related cooling or 2025 sets a substantially higher threshold. It could be too low if strong El Niño conditions or persistent exceptional ocean warmth elevate 2026 temperatures. Although the cutoff is in September 2026, no year-to-date observations are supplied, so this estimate cannot benefit from the substantial information that would normally be available by then.
limitations: No outside evidence records or current research were supplied, and browsing is unavailable.
The NASA GISS 2025 annual value and 2026 monthly observations are unavailable here.
Current ENSO conditions and forecasts are not established by the supplied evidence.
The strict comparison depends on the contract-relevant NASA series and its reported precision; alternative temperature datasets are not interchangeable.
